questions.explanation: Immunodiagnostic (serological/antigen-detection) methods are especially valuable in bancroftian filariasis when microfilariae cannot be directly demonstrated in blood -- during the prepatent period (before microfilaremia develops), in chronic infection with amicrofilaremia, and in tropical pulmonary eosinophilia (an immune hyperresponsiveness syndrome where microfilariae are typically absent from peripheral blood).
questions.keyConcept: Immunodiagnosis is most valuable precisely when microfilariae are undetectable in blood -- prepatent, amicrofilaremic chronic, and TPE cases.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which factors one is NOT of the affected following by warfarin: clotting
questions.explanation: Adult Wuchereria bancrofti worms inhabit the lymphatics of the lower limbs, groin, and scrotum -- not the upper limb below the elbow. Nocturnal periodicity of microfilariae, Culex as a vector, elephantiasis, and chyluria are all true features of bancroftian filariasis.
questions.keyConcept: Adult W. bancrofti worms characteristically inhabit lower-limb and genital lymphatics, not the upper limb.

questions.keyConcept: Dabigatran is an oral direct thrombin inhibitor; idarucizumab is its specific reversal agent; for “Which of the following is a direct thrombin inhibitor given orally”, the defining choice is “Argatroban”.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: A 45-year man presented to outpatient clinic with fever, severe pain in joints with rash. He was in West Africa & came back two weeks ago. Causative agent could be ____ 0
questions.explanation: A key teaching point about dengue is that infection with a new (heterotypic) serotype after a prior dengue infection can trigger antibody-dependent enhancement, leading to severe hemorrhage and shock (dengue hemorrhagic fever/dengue shock syndrome). Dengue is mosquito-borne (not rodent-borne), and there is no widely available, fully effective vaccine used in routine practice in most teaching contexts.
questions.keyConcept: Secondary infection with a different dengue serotype can trigger severe hemorrhagic disease via antibody-dependent enhancement.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: A 45-year man presented to the outpatient clinic with fever, severe pain in muscle & joints with rash. He was in Ghana & came back two weeks ago. Which investigation do you recommend the to conhrm the diagnosis?
options: Detection of viral antigens by IF
RT-PCR for detection of viral RNA
Detection of viral particles in serum using EM
questions.explanation: Animal inoculation (e.g., into mice or guinea pigs) is used to detect Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense, which is more virulent and produces higher, more easily detectable parasitemia in inoculated animals than the chronic, low-parasitemia T. b. gambiense infection. This technique is not typically needed for T. cruzi or Plasmodium falciparum, which have other characteristic diagnostic methods.
questions.keyConcept: Animal inoculation is a sensitive diagnostic method for T. b. rhodesiense, which produces high, easily detectable parasitemia in test animals.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: A patient came to the emergency room suffering from fever, myalgia & bleeding, on examination his blood pressure was markedly low, also multiple red dots "petechiae" were found on his skin, it was reported that he was diagnesed 3 years ago with dengue fever, all following statements are true EXCEPT:
options: this patient can't be suffering from dengue fever as he was already infected 3 years ago & he is immune against it
the patient is suffering from dengue shock syndrome as a result of reinfection with another serotype of dengue fever virus
there's no cross immunity between DEN-1 & DEN-2 serotypes
reinfection with another serotype of dengue fever virus increase the chance of developing dengue hemorrhagic fever symptoms
questions.explanation: Dengue virus is unique among these hemorrhagic fever viruses in that infection with a second, different serotype causes more severe disease (dengue hemorrhagic fever/shock syndrome) due to antibody-dependent enhancement; yellow fever, Ebola, and Marburg do not have this well-defined multi-serotype enhancement phenomenon.
questions.keyConcept: Only dengue among these viruses shows serotype-dependent enhancement of disease severity on reinfection.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: African hemorrhagic fevers, Marburg Ebola, are severe diseases often ending in death. Which of the following is true about Ebola virus?
options: Causes infections but no disease in nonhuman primates
Serology is the main tool for diagnosis
Spread by contact with blood or other body fluids
questions.explanation: Fruit bats are the suspected natural reservoir host for Ebola virus, not cattle, monkeys, or sheep, which can become infected but are not the reservoir.
questions.keyConcept: Bats are the suspected natural reservoir of Ebola virus.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: All of the followings are true about yellow fever virus EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: Parvovirus B19 has no recognized arthropod vector; it spreads via respiratory secretions, blood/blood products, and vertical (mother-to-fetus) transmission, all of which are established routes.
questions.keyConcept: Parvovirus B19 transmission does not involve an arthropod vector.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: An Egyptian farmer came to the local health center complaining of weakness, myalgia & vision problems, his wife of reported this happened a week after he was working at his farm as many heads of cows have died, his diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Infection with one dengue serotype confers lifelong immunity only to that specific serotype; immunity against the other three serotypes is not durable, which is why later infection with a different serotype can occur and even be more severe.
questions.keyConcept: Dengue serotype immunity is lifelong only for the infecting serotype, not cross-protective long term.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Dengue virus has four distinct serotypes. Infection with one serotype provides:
options: Lifelong immunity to all four serotypes
Lifelong immunity to only that specific serotype
Temporary immunity to all serotypes about a year
No immunity, making reinfection more likely and less severe
questions.explanation: For an acute arboviral febrile illness (fever, severe myalgia/arthralgia, rash) shortly after travel, RT-PCR detection of viral RNA is the most sensitive and standard confirmatory test during the early viremic phase, before antibody responses have developed.
questions.keyConcept: RT-PCR for viral RNA is the preferred confirmatory test during the early viremic phase of arboviral infections.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Ebola virus is usually transmitted by
questions.explanation: Ebola virus spreads through direct contact with the blood or other body fluids of infected individuals, not by mosquito bite. Bats, not rodents, are the suspected natural reservoir, and PCR (not serology) is the main diagnostic tool during acute infection.
questions.keyConcept: Ebola is transmitted by direct contact with infected body fluids.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Ebola virus reservoir host is:
questions.explanation: Marburg and Ebola viruses (filoviruses, not flaviviruses) characteristically cause severe gastrointestinal bleeding and hepatic involvement. They are not prevented by the 17D (yellow fever) vaccine, are transmitted human-to-human via contact with body fluids (not arthropods), so the other statements are false.
questions.keyConcept: Marburg and Ebola are filoviruses causing severe hemorrhagic GI and hepatic disease, transmitted by direct contact, not arthropods.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: One reason cited for the absence of reported Yellow Fever cases in Egypt is the cross-immunity with which other flavivirus?
questions.explanation: Yellow fever virus is a Flavivirus, not a filovirus (filoviruses are Ebola and Marburg), making this the false statement. It is genuinely prevented by the live-attenuated 17D vaccine, causes jaundice and renal involvement, and is transmitted by mosquitoes.
questions.keyConcept: Yellow fever virus belongs to the Flavivirus family, not the filoviruses.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Rift Valley Fever is a zoonotic disease primarily pathogenic for sheep and of cattle. Humans are secondarily mental infected through: rural
options: The bite of an infected mosquito or exposure to infected animal fluids
The bite of an infected tick
questions.explanation: Rift Valley Fever is transmitted by mosquito bite as well as by direct contact with the blood or fluids of infected sheep and cattle, distinguishing it from the other listed hemorrhagic fevers.
questions.keyConcept: Rift Valley Fever spreads via both mosquito bite and direct contact with infected livestock fluids.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Which of the following groups is considered at high risk for person-to- person transmission of Ebola?
options: Healthcare workers and mourners at burial ceremonies
Farmers working with cattle and sheep
questions.explanation: Ebola virus is usually transmitted through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person or animal, not by mosquito bite, droplet spread, or direct transmission from cattle.
questions.keyConcept: Ebola virus transmission is via direct contact with infected blood/body fluids, not through an insect vector.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Which of the following is true regarding Dengue fever virus:
questions.explanation: In the urban transmission cycle of dengue, humans serve as the primary reservoir and amplifying host, with Aedes mosquitoes acting only as the vector (not a reservoir).
questions.keyConcept: Humans are the main reservoir host for dengue virus in the urban transmission cycle.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Which of the following isn't true jungle yellow fever?
options: Is transmitted accidentally to man by Mosquitoes
Man to man transmission occurs by droplet
There is affection of liver& kidney
questions.explanation: Jaundice with black vomitus ('vomito negro') in a traveler after a safari (jungle/forest exposure) is the classic description of jungle (sylvatic) yellow fever, transmitted by forest-dwelling Aedes mosquitoes from a monkey reservoir.
questions.keyConcept: Jaundice with black vomitus after jungle/forest exposure is the hallmark presentation of jungle yellow fever.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Which of the following may increase the severity of the above disease?
options: Previous infection with another virus the same family
Previous infection with another of the same virus
questions.explanation: Dengue immunity is serotype-specific, so a person previously infected with one dengue serotype is not immune to other serotypes and can still develop dengue (often more severely) upon reinfection — making the claim that he 'can't be suffering from dengue' the false statement. The other statements about dengue shock syndrome from serotype reinfection, lack of cross-immunity between DEN-1 and DEN-2, and increased DHF risk on reinfection are all true.
questions.keyConcept: Dengue immunity is serotype-specific; prior infection does not protect against other serotypes.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Which of the following viruses, known to be associated with hemorrhagic fever, more severe disease if the patient is subsequently infected with another serotype of the same virus?
questions.explanation: Dengue hemorrhagic fever/dengue shock syndrome is the classic example of immunopathology among viral hemorrhagic fevers, arising from antibody-dependent enhancement during secondary infection with a different dengue serotype.
questions.keyConcept: Dengue hemorrhagic fever is driven by immunopathology (antibody-dependent enhancement), unlike Ebola, Marburg, or yellow fever.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Which of the followings is true about Marburg & Ebola viruses?
options: Characterized by severe GIT bleeding & hepatic affection
Not transmitted from human to human
questions.explanation: Humans become secondarily infected with Rift Valley Fever virus mainly through the bite of an infected mosquito or through direct exposure to the blood or body fluids of infected animals (such as sheep and cattle), not through person-to-person respiratory spread, undercooked pork, or ticks.
questions.keyConcept: Human RVF infection occurs via mosquito bite or contact with infected animal fluids, not person-to-person spread.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Which one of the following viral is transmitted by blood sucking & contact with sheep & cattle?
questions.explanation: The severity of dengue disease is most classically increased by prior infection with a different dengue serotype of the same virus, which triggers antibody-dependent enhancement rather than protective immunity.
questions.keyConcept: Heterotypic dengue serotype reinfection, not simple prior exposure to the same family, drives severe disease via antibody-dependent enhancement.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: While most cases of Rift Valley diseases Fever are mild, a small proportion insect of patients can develop severe syndromes, including:
options: Arthritis and a spreading annular rash
questions.explanation: Weakness, myalgia, and ocular/vision complications in an Egyptian farmer following unexplained deaths among his cattle is a classic presentation of Rift Valley Fever, a mosquito-borne zoonosis affecting livestock with occasional ocular complications (retinitis) in humans.
questions.keyConcept: Rift Valley Fever in farmers presents with systemic illness and characteristic ocular complications after livestock die-offs.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Adhesion of platelets to damaged endothelium is mainly due to the presence of:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because the platelet glycocalyx (thick cell coat) carries surface glycoproteins important for adhesion to injured vascular surfaces. Filaments and canaliculi serve other structural or secretory roles.
questions.keyConcept: Platelet-released ADP promotes recruitment and aggregation of additional platelets through positive feedback; for “Adhesion of platelets to damaged endothelium is mainly due to the presence of”, the defining choice is “Thick cell coat”.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Alpha granules in platelets contain the following except:
questions.explanation: Fibrin degradation products (FDPs), generated when plasmin breaks down fibrin clots, have an anticoagulant feedback effect: they inhibit thrombin activity (and interfere with fibrin polymerization), helping limit excessive clot propagation once fibrinolysis begins.
questions.keyConcept: FDPs from clot lysis feed back to inhibit thrombin, limiting further clot propagation.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Delta granules of platelets contain the following except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because dense (delta) granules contain small molecules such as ADP, ATP, calcium, and serotonin. Fibrinogen is stored in alpha granules instead.
questions.keyConcept: Platelet-released ADP promotes recruitment and aggregation of additional platelets through positive feedback; for “Delta granules of platelets contain the following except”, the defining choice is “Fibrinogen”.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: In blood platelets, calcium is stored mainly in the:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because the dense tubular system of platelets is analogous to smooth endoplasmic reticulum and functions as a calcium store. Open canalicular channels are for communication/secretion rather than calcium storage.
questions.keyConcept: Platelet-released ADP promotes recruitment and aggregation of additional platelets through positive feedback; for “In blood platelets, calcium is stored mainly in the”, the defining choice is “Dense tubular system”.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Lysis of the blood clot is one platelet function. Which structure is responsible for that?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because lambda granules are lysosome-like granules containing hydrolytic enzymes involved in clot remodeling and lysis. Alpha and dense granules store other mediators instead.
questions.keyConcept: Serum is plasma minus the clotting factors consumed during coagulation (mainly fibrinogen), obtained after clot formation.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Nuclei of megakaryocytes are characterized by being:
questions.explanation: The normal platelet count in adults is approximately 150,000-400,000/mm3 (commonly cited teaching range 100-400 x10^3/mm3); counts below this range define thrombocytopenia, which increases bleeding risk, particularly when counts fall below about 50,000/mm3.
questions.keyConcept: Normal platelet count is roughly 150,000-400,000/mm3; values below this define thrombocytopenia.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Release of coagulation factors from platelets is facilitated by the:
questions.explanation: Factor V Leiden is a point mutation in factor V that makes it resistant to inactivation by activated protein C, so the normal anticoagulant brake on factor Va is lost, prolonging procoagulant activity and predisposing to venous thrombosis -- it is a hereditary hypercoagulable state, not a factor V deficiency, liver disease, or platelet disorder, and does not cause bleeding.
questions.keyConcept: Factor V Leiden confers resistance to activated protein C, causing a hereditary hypercoagulable (pro-thrombotic) state.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: The discoid/ovoid shape of platelets is maintained by:
questions.explanation: Prothrombin time (PT) specifically evaluates the extrinsic pathway (factor VII) and the common pathway, making it the test of choice for monitoring warfarin therapy and assessing extrinsic-pathway factor deficiencies, as opposed to aPTT, which evaluates the intrinsic pathway.
questions.keyConcept: PT tests the extrinsic and common coagulation pathways, distinct from aPTT, which tests the intrinsic pathway.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: The megakaryocyte is the precursor cell of:
questions.explanation: Blood performs homeostatic functions (maintaining stable internal conditions), hemostasis (clotting to stop bleeding), and temperature regulation (via heat distribution/dissipation) -- but it plays no role in adjusting skin pigmentation, which is determined by melanocyte activity, not blood composition.
questions.keyConcept: Blood contributes to homeostasis, hemostasis, and thermoregulation, but not skin pigmentation, which is melanocyte-dependent.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: The platelet contains microtubules and actin filaments in the:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because the platelet peripheral zone (hyalomere) contains the circumferential microtubule band and actin-myosin system that maintain shape and permit contraction. The central zone contains the granules and organelles.
questions.keyConcept: Platelet-released ADP promotes recruitment and aggregation of additional platelets through positive feedback; for “The platelet contains microtubules and actin filaments in the”, the defining choice is “Peripheral zone”.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following is the best description of platelets?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because platelets are small anucleate cytoplasmic fragments derived from megakaryocytes and appear discoid/biconvex when inactive. They are not complete nucleated cells.
questions.keyConcept: Platelet-released ADP promotes recruitment and aggregation of additional platelets through positive feedback; for “Which of the following is the best description of platelets”, the defining choice is “Biconvex fragments”.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which platelet granules contain ATP and calcium?
questions.explanation: Bleeding time specifically tests the vascular and platelet phases of hemostasis (vasoconstriction and platelet plug formation), making it abnormal in vascular or platelet disorders (e.g., thrombocytopenia) while remaining normal in isolated coagulation factor deficiencies, unlike PT or aPTT, which test the coagulation cascade itself.
questions.keyConcept: Bleeding time isolates vascular/platelet function, whereas PT and aPTT test the coagulation factor cascade.

questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which type of platelet granules contains hydrolytic enzymes?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because lambda granules are lysosomal granules that contain hydrolytic enzymes. Alpha and delta granules contain secretory mediators instead.
questions.keyConcept: Platelet-released ADP promotes recruitment and aggregation of additional platelets through positive feedback; for “Which type of platelet granules contains hydrolytic enzymes”, the defining choice is “Lambda granules”.
